title: Hooke's law
statement: recall and use Hooke's law

title: Spring constant, k = F/x
statement: recall and use the formula for the spring constant $k = F/x$

title: Stress, strain and Young modulus
statement: define and use the terms stress, strain and the Young modulus

title: Measuring the Young modulus of a wire
statement: describe an experiment to determine the Young modulus of a metal in the form of a wire

title: Elastic and plastic deformation
statement: understand and use the terms elastic deformation, plastic deformation and elastic limit

title: Work done from a force-extension graph
statement: understand that the area under the force–extension graph represents the work done

title: Elastic potential energy from a graph
statement: determine the elastic potential energy of a material deformed within its limit of proportionality from the area under the force–extension graph

title: Elastic potential energy formulas
statement: recall and use $E_P = \frac{1}{2}Fx = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$ for a material deformed within its limit of proportionality

title: Describing wave motion
statement: describe what is meant by wave motion as illustrated by vibration in ropes, springs and ripple tanks

title: Wave terms: amplitude, period, wavelength
statement: understand and use the terms displacement, amplitude, phase difference, period, frequency, wavelength and speed

title: Using a CRO for frequency and amplitude
statement: understand the use of the time-base and y-gain of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) to determine frequency and amplitude

title: Deriving the wave equation
statement: derive, using the definitions of speed, frequency and wavelength, the wave equation $v = f\lambda$

title: Using the wave equation, v = fλ
statement: recall and use $v = f\lambda$

title: Energy transfer by a progressive wave
statement: understand that energy is transferred by a progressive wave

title: Wave intensity and amplitude
statement: recall and use $\text{intensity} = \text{power}/\text{area}$ and $\text{intensity} \propto (\text{amplitude})^2$ for a progressive wave

title: Transverse versus longitudinal waves
statement: compare transverse and longitudinal waves

title: Interpreting wave graphs
statement: analyse and interpret graphical representations of transverse and longitudinal waves

title: Doppler effect, moving source
statement: understand that when a source of sound waves moves relative to a stationary observer, the observed frequency is different from the source frequency (understanding of the Doppler effect for a stationary source and a moving observer is not required)

title: Doppler effect frequency formula
statement: use the expression $f_o = \dfrac{f_s v}{v \pm v_s}$ for the observed frequency when a source of sound waves moves relative to a stationary observer
glossary: fo = fsv over v plus or minus vs

title: Electromagnetic waves travel at speed c
statement: state that all electromagnetic waves are transverse waves that travel with the same speed c in free space

title: Electromagnetic spectrum wavelength ranges
statement: recall the approximate range of wavelengths in free space of the principal regions of the electromagnetic spectrum from radio waves to γ-rays

title: Visible light wavelength range
statement: recall that wavelengths in the range 400–700 nm in free space are visible to the human eye

title: Polarisation of transverse waves
statement: understand that polarisation is a phenomenon associated with transverse waves

title: Malus's law for polarised intensity
statement: recall and use Malus's law ($I = I_0 \cos^2\theta$) to calculate the intensity of a plane-polarised electromagnetic wave after transmission through a polarising filter or a series of polarising filters (calculation of the effect of a polarising filter on the intensity of an unpolarised wave is not required)

title: Principle of superposition
statement: explain and use the principle of superposition

title: Demonstrating stationary waves
statement: show an understanding of experiments that demonstrate stationary waves using microwaves, stretched strings and air columns (it will be assumed that end corrections are negligible; knowledge of the concept of end corrections is not required)

title: Formation of a stationary wave
statement: explain the formation of a stationary wave using a graphical method, and identify nodes and antinodes

title: Wavelength from nodes and antinodes
statement: understand how wavelength may be determined from the positions of nodes or antinodes of a stationary wave

title: Meaning of diffraction
statement: explain the meaning of the term diffraction

title: Demonstrating diffraction
statement: show an understanding of experiments that demonstrate diffraction including the qualitative effect of the gap width relative to the wavelength of the wave; for example diffraction of water waves in a ripple tank
